# Observer Pattern Explained

## What Is It?

The **Observer pattern** defines a **one-to-many dependency** between objects. When the **subject** (also called "Observable") changes state, all its **observers** are automatically notified and updated.

```
┌─────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐
│   Subject   │────────▶│     Observer 1   │
│  (Stock)    │ notify  │                  │
│             │────────▶│     Observer 2   │
│ + attach()  │         │                  │
│ + detach()  │────────▶│     Observer 3   │
│ + notify()  │         │                  │
└─────────────┘         └──────────────────┘
```

---

## TypeScript Example: Stock Price Monitor

```typescript
// ============================================
// INTERFACES
// ============================================

interface Observer {
  update(subject: Subject): void;
}

interface Subject {
  attach(observer: Observer): void;
  detach(observer: Observer): void;
  notify(): void;
}

// ============================================
// CONCRETE SUBJECT: Stock Price Tracker
// ============================================

class Stock implements Subject
